project.name: SystemViz
project.author: Peter Stoyko
project.description: A research project exploring how visuals can enhance systems thinking, especially as it relates to inter-disciplinary, collaborative design.
project.book: How Small Players Change Big Systems (Peter Stoyko, forthcoming)

pillars.name: Visual Vocabulary of Systems
pillars.description: A codex of the main elements and dynamics of systems, assembled from an extensive review of natural sciences, social sciences, design, and managerial disciplines. Each item has an illustrative icon.
awards: IIID Award (top-tier, International Institute for Information Design)

pillars.name: Pattern Atlas of System Vulnerabilities
pillars.description: Uses the 'tangle' metaphor to explain weaknesses inherent to elaborate human-made systems, identifying ~30 types of systemic vulnerability across four levels of scale.

pillars.name: Anatomy of System Notations
pillars.description: A comprehensive inventory (codex) of graphical devices used in visual system notations, drawn from 70 existing notations.

pillars.name: ESCALADE Information-Design Framework
pillars.description: Eight marquee criteria for improving system diagrams, maps, notations, and other graphics. Explained in a series of slide-notes with additional tips and considerations.

visual_vocabulary.description: The core lexicon of system elements and dynamics. 6 categories, 56 terms with full definitions from the published vocabulary, plus 30 CA-extension terms developed for the mito-aging simulator project.
visual_vocabulary.note_on_coverage: The full VV v1.3.0 contains 200 elements. This lexicon includes all 56 core terms with published definitions, 30 project-specific CA extensions, and 15 additional VV terms identified from version notes (definitions pending, site currently offline).

driver.description: The active cause of some happening within the system.

control_point.definition: Contact between a subject and object whereby power or influence can be exerted.

conduit.definition: A path along which actors are expected to move.

amplifier.definition: A combination of factors or process that increases the magnitude of an effect.

repeller.definition: An object that pushes other objects away from itself.

enabler.definition: A contributory cause; can encourage change.

dampener.definition: A combination of factors or process that reduces the magnitude of an effect.

cycle.definition: A repeating process or iterative effort towards a goal.

genator.definition: The original impetus or trigger of a sequence of events.

cascade.definition: A sequence of knock-on effects; a chain reaction.

inflection.definition: A turning point or critical juncture.

equifinality.definition: Multiple activities lead to the same outcome.

side_effect.definition: An unintended consequence of an action on a different part of the system.
side_effect.note: Not in published VV lexicon; inferred from simulator mapping

signal.description: Communication that can potentially trigger some action.

framing.definition: Interpretive paradigm which makes the system understandable.

monitor.definition: Active scanning of a process or domain to compare with an expected state.

indicator.definition: Indirect or partial signal of status; a symptom of a deeper cause.

feed_back.definition: Information about the outputs of an action are routed back as inputs.

status_display.definition: Regularly updated information about a particular object.

alert.definition: A warning signal intended to mobilize a response.

state.description: A condition of a system or objects within it.

stock.definition: A discrete collection of consumable or expendable resources for future use.

standard.definition: A set of items made more or less uniform; conformity to criteria.

redundancy.definition: Multiple stockpiles or parallel sub-systems that act as a back-up.

fault_recovery.definition: Correction or compensation that minimize impact of faults.

tipping_point.definition: The threshold beyond which rapid, large-scale change happens.

criticality.definition: The threshold beyond which a dynamic becomes self-sustaining.

load.definition: A stock of items being moved under containment conditions.

mutation.definition: A reconfiguration of an object caused by an error or exogenous factor.

transition.definition: Changing from one state to another.

accumulation.definition: The build-up of items or experiences over time.

capacity.definition: The finite ability to handle a particular quantity of activity.

reset.definition: Returning to original conditions or earlier state.

replication.definition: When an object is copied, reproduced, or divided.

assembly.definition: Building blocks with which system structures are formed.

separation.definition: The division of a part into two or more parts.

maintenance.definition: The restoration of operations after a malfunction.

fault.definition: A defect or malfunction in a system component.
fault.note: Not in published VV lexicon; inferred from simulator mapping

boundary.description: Separates different parts of a system.

gate.definition: A controlled opening in a barrier.

buffer.definition: A boundary or zone that diminishes, delays, or otherwise alters a driver.

reactive_boundary.definition: A boundary that responds to forces and acts as an actant.

permissions.definition: The control of activity within a bounded area.

container.definition: A boundary that groups and isolates objects.

semi_permiable.definition: A barrier that blocks some objects while allowing others.

divider.definition: A boundary that keeps two or more distinct objects apart.

protector.definition: A barrier preventing damage by blocking unwanted forces.

edge.definition: Outer boundary that defines the scope of domain or system.

relation.description: The dynamic between two or more objects in a system.

group.definition: An affiliated collective of actors that share patterns of behavior.

rank.definition: The hierarchical status bestowed on an object or actor.

differentiation.definition: A contrast between other items or actors in a system.

mediation.definition: The mitigation or reconciliation of conflict between parties.

aggregate.definition: A group of objects or actors of the same type.

coupling.definition: The tightness or looseness of ties between parts of a system.

network.definition: An arrangement of interconnected parts that interact directly.

cluster.definition: Elements defined as a group by virtue of proximity.

domain.description: The context in which the system (or parts thereof) exists.

reference_points.definition: Features in the context that can act as orienting devices.

resources.definition: The availability and access to the factor inputs needed.

levels_of_scale.definition: System attributes at different orders of analysis.

ca_extensions.description: Terms added for the Semantic Cellular Automaton layer. These extend the VV categories with discrete-state concepts used in the mito-aging simulator's CA model.

ca.attractor.definition: A stable state or trajectory toward which the CA system converges.

ca.attractor_transition.definition: A shift from one attractor basin to another, driven by parameter changes or rule cascades.

ca.bin_lattice.definition: The structured arrangement of discretization bins forming the CA state space.

ca.bin_ordering.definition: The ordinal relationship between bins (e.g., minimal < growing < approaching_cliff < past_cliff).

ca.bin_state.definition: The discrete bin assignment of a continuous variable at a given timestep.

ca.bin_threshold.definition: The numeric cutpoint between adjacent bins in the discretization schema.

ca.bin_transition.definition: The event of a variable crossing from one bin to an adjacent bin.

ca.cascade.definition: A chain of rule firings where the output of one rule triggers the input conditions for another.

ca.cliff_boundary.definition: The heteroplasmy threshold (deletion het ~0.50) beyond which ATP collapses nonlinearly.

ca.cliff_crossing_signal.definition: A bin transition indicating that deletion heteroplasmy has crossed the cliff threshold.

ca.discrete_state.definition: The full tuple of bin assignments across all 8 ODE variables at one timestep.

ca.rule_firing.definition: The activation of a tiered transition rule when its input bin conditions are satisfied.

ca.state_space.definition: The complete set of possible discrete states (11,664 in the mito-aging CA).

ca.variable_coupling.definition: The dependency between variables captured by multi-input rule conditions.

pattern_atlas.description: The Pattern Atlas of System Vulnerabilities uses the 'tangle' metaphor to explain weaknesses inherent to elaborate, human-made systems.
pattern_atlas.confidence: category names confirmed from PDF title/search results; individual pattern assignments are provisional (source PDFs inaccessible)

levels_of_scale.description: Vulnerabilities operate at four nested levels of analysis.

levels.name: Component
levels.description: Individual parts or elements within a subsystem.

levels.name: Subsystem
levels.description: Functional groupings of components that serve a specific purpose.

levels.name: System
levels.description: The complete operational entity with defined boundaries.

levels.name: System of Systems
levels.description: Interconnected independent systems that together produce emergent behavior.

vulnerability_categories.description: Seven high-level categories of systemic vulnerability, each containing multiple specific patterns.

categories.name: UNIFORM
categories.description: Vulnerability arising from excessive homogeneity or standardization, reducing adaptive capacity.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads all the same — no diversity to absorb shocks.

categories.name: UNTETHERED
categories.description: Vulnerability from disconnection, lack of grounding, or absence of stabilizing connections.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads floating free — no anchor points.

categories.name: PROPPED UP
categories.description: Vulnerability from artificial supports that mask underlying structural weakness.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads held up by fragile props — collapse when props fail.

categories.name: OVEREXTENDED
categories.description: Vulnerability from operating beyond sustainable capacity or reach.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads stretched too far — snapping under tension.

categories.name: PRECARIOUS
categories.description: Vulnerability from unstable equilibria or positions that small perturbations can topple.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads balanced on edge — any push tips them.

categories.name: ENSNARLING
categories.description: Vulnerability from excessive entanglement, creating unintended dependencies and lock-in.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads wound too tight — pulling one disrupts many.

categories.name: SPIRALING
categories.description: Vulnerability from self-reinforcing feedback loops that amplify deviations.
categories.tangle_metaphor: Threads coiling inward — accelerating toward breakdown.

anatomy_codex.description: The Anatomy of System Notations: a comprehensive inventory of graphical devices used in visual system notations.
anatomy_codex.confidence: structure confirmed from RSD Symposium publication; individual device catalog requires access to PDF/poster

device_categories.description: Graphical devices are grouped by the system concepts they represent.
device_categories.note: Categories listed here are inferred from standard systems notation literature and the SystemViz VV category structure. Detailed taxonomy requires the full codex document.

categories.name: Element Representation
categories.description: Devices for depicting system objects, actors, and components (shapes, icons, labels).

categories.name: Boundary Depiction
categories.description: Devices for showing system boundaries, containers, membranes, and scope (enclosures, dotted lines, shading).

categories.name: Flow and Connection
categories.description: Devices for showing relationships, flows, and connections between elements (arrows, lines, connectors).

categories.name: Feedback and Loops
categories.description: Devices for depicting feedback loops, cycles, and recursive processes (circular arrows, polarity markers).

categories.name: State and Dynamics
categories.description: Devices for representing states, transitions, stocks, and accumulations (reservoirs, valves, level indicators).

categories.name: Hierarchy and Nesting
categories.description: Devices for showing levels of scale, decomposition, and containment (nesting, tree structures, layers).

categories.name: Annotation and Metadata
categories.description: Devices for adding explanatory information, labels, legends, and qualitative markers (color coding, typography, icons).

source_notation_families.description: The 70 source notations span multiple disciplinary traditions.

escalade.description: ESCALADE: An information-design framework of eight marquee criteria for improving system diagrams, maps, notations, and other graphics. Most system graphics are developed without any consideration to design criteria; ESCALADE fills that gap.
escalade.confidence: framework existence and 8-criteria structure confirmed; individual criterion names provisional (site offline, slide-notes inaccessible)

criteria.note: The ESCALADE acronym encodes 8 criteria. The names below are reconstructed from available web search fragments and standard information design vocabulary. Definitions should be verified against the published slide-notes when systemviz.com is restored.

provisional_criteria.name: Expressiveness
provisional_criteria.description: The notation should be capable of representing the full range of system concepts required.

provisional_criteria.name: Simplicity
provisional_criteria.description: Graphics should use the minimum visual complexity needed to convey the intended meaning.

provisional_criteria.name: Consistency
provisional_criteria.description: Visual conventions should be applied uniformly throughout the diagram.

provisional_criteria.name: Adaptability
provisional_criteria.description: The notation should accommodate different system types, scales, and domains.

provisional_criteria.name: Legibility
provisional_criteria.description: Elements should be visually distinct and readable at intended viewing distances.

provisional_criteria.name: Accuracy
provisional_criteria.description: Visual representations should faithfully reflect the underlying system structure and dynamics.

provisional_criteria.name: Distinction
provisional_criteria.description: Different types of elements and relationships should be visually distinguishable.

provisional_criteria.name: Elegance
provisional_criteria.description: The overall composition should achieve aesthetic coherence that supports comprehension.

cross_pillar_relations.description: Structural connections between the four SystemViz pillars.

relations.description: The VV elements are rendered using graphical devices cataloged in the Codex. Each VV icon is assembled from Codex-documented visual primitives.
VV terms describe the system dynamics that vulnerability patterns exploit. For example, 'cascade' (VV driver) describes the propagation mechanism in 'SPIRALING' vulnerability patterns.
The 65 graphical devices from 70 notations can be evaluated against the 8 ESCALADE criteria to assess their design quality.
Atlas vulnerability patterns are diagrammed using VV icons and notation conventions.
ESCALADE criteria govern the design quality of VV icons and the syntax rules for their composition.

vv_to_atlas_mapping.description: How VV terms map to Pattern Atlas vulnerability categories.

mappings.note: Redundancy counteracts the uniformity vulnerability through diversity.
Cascades are the propagation mechanism of spiraling vulnerabilities.
Tipping points mark where precarious equilibria collapse.
Buffers prevent overextension by absorbing excess demand.
Tight coupling creates the entanglement that ensnarling exploits.
Genuine fault recovery replaces artificial propping-up.
Support structures provide the grounding that untethered systems lack.

lakoff_archetypes.description: Lakoff conceptual metaphor mappings for intervention protocol classification. Each archetype represents a different cognitive framing of the intervention strategy.

conservative.description: Low-risk, maintenance-focused intervention with minimal energy cost.

aggressive.description: High-intensity intervention aiming for damage reversal.

transplant_focused.description: Protocol centered on mtDNA transplant as primary rejuvenation.

metabolic_optimizer.description: Protocol optimizing metabolic flexibility via combined interventions.

simulator_mappings.description: How components of the mito-aging simulator map to VV terms. Enables SystemViz-compatible diagramming of simulation architecture.

pattern_language_bridge.description: How this lexicon connects to a SystemViz-compatible pattern language for a new project. The VV categories map to pattern language stages.

stage_mapping.role: Establishes the operating environment, resources, and scale of the system.
Defines containment, connections, and organizational relationships.
Captures active forces, conditions, and state changes.
Identifies structural weaknesses using the Atlas taxonomy.
Evaluates diagram and notation quality using ESCALADE criteria.
